convoLines.text: "They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Arjun. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"We lost Tyler and Marisol this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Alright. Catch you later."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"Tyler is gone and Marisol is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"I keep turning over the last thing Marisol said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Marisol. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the meadow edge, west of the creek in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about Lockpick last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"My part? I rinse the cup twice and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I froze when it mattered. I think about it every day."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Lockpick? Arjun is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on each other."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the north treeline by the fallen oak — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on each other."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Actually, forget it."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
"The pantry run — I haven't stopped thinking about it."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the meadow edge, west of the creek in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
As I said — There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took you — The Maw, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Arjun doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Anyway — I should get going."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything. I'm listening."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it. Just thinking out loud."
"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"Still on what you believe in."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The Maw. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Same as always: we endure."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
